name: GPS Broadcast Path & Ledger Depth Flywheel
description: Drives operator activation and upgrade conversion through a zero-auth driver PWA that broadcasts GPS pings, anchors each ping to a Hyperledger Fabric ledger transaction, instruments V/T ratio coverage via PostHog, delivers time-gated SMS nudges via Upstash Redis for operators who have not yet received a first GPS ping, and surfaces a compliance-framed free-tier ledger gate at Day 28 to convert operators to paid plans. The flywheel completes when a first GPS ping unlocks full navigation, writes a ledger genesis event, and begins the countdown to the upgrade gate — creating a compounding retention and monetization loop.

functions.name: enqueuePing
functions.logic: Accepts a GPSPingPayload object containing latitude, longitude, accuracy, timestamp, device_token, and vehicle_id. Opens the IndexedDB 'gps_queue' object store and adds the ping as a new record with an auto-incremented key. If IndexedDB is unavailable, falls back to localStorage with a serialised JSON array. Does not throw on storage failure — logs a console warning instead to avoid disrupting the driver UI. Returns void.

functions.name: flushQueue
functions.signature: flushQueue(ingestUrl: string): Promise<{ flushed: number; failed: number }>
functions.logic: Reads all records from the IndexedDB 'gps_queue' object store in insertion order. For each record, POSTs the ping payload to ingestUrl with a JSON body and Bearer device_token header. On HTTP 200 or 201, deletes the record from IndexedDB. On network error or non-2xx response, retains the record for the next flush attempt and increments the failed counter. Returns an object with flushed (count of successfully sent pings) and failed (count of pings that remain queued). Registers a 'online' event listener on window to auto-invoke flushQueue when connectivity is restored.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Parses the JSON body expecting fields: device_token (string), vehicle_id (string), latitude (number), longitude (number), accuracy (number), timestamp (ISO string), route_corridor (string, optional). Validates device_token against the devices table in PostgreSQL — returns 401 if not found or revoked. Inserts a row into trip_events with vehicle_id, latitude, longitude, accuracy, timestamp, route_corridor, and a boolean accuracy_flag set to true when accuracy > 50. Enqueues a Hyperledger Fabric write job by calling writeTripEvent with the inserted row. Checks if this is the first ping for the operator by querying trip_events count for the org — if count equals 1, calls cancelNudgeJobs(operator_id) to cancel pending SMS nudge jobs in Upstash Redis, and emits a PostHog event 'gps_first_ping_received' with operator_id and vehicle_id. Returns JSON 201 with the inserted event id.

functions.name: writeTripEvent
functions.signature: writeTripEvent(event: TripEventRecord): Promise<{ txId: string; success: boolean }>
functions.logic: Accepts a TripEventRecord with fields: id, vehicle_id, route_corridor, latitude, longitude, accuracy, accuracy_flag, timestamp. Connects to the Hyperledger Fabric gateway using the pre-configured identity wallet and channel name from environment variables FABRIC_CHANNEL and FABRIC_CHAINCODE. Constructs a ledger transaction payload JSON-encoding all fields plus a unix epoch timestamp. Calls contract.submitTransaction('WriteTripEvent', JSON.stringify(payload)) and awaits the result. On success, returns { txId: transactionId, success: true }. On Fabric SDK error, logs the error with the event id and retries once after a 500ms delay. If the retry also fails, writes the event to a dead-letter PostgreSQL table 'fabric_dlq' for manual reprocessing and returns { txId: null, success: false }. This ensures the GPS ping ingest endpoint is never blocked by Fabric latency.

functions.name: computeVTRatio
functions.signature: computeVTRatio(vehicleId: string, date: string): Promise<{ vehicle_id: string; date: string; vt_ratio: number; actual_trips: number; expected_trips: number }>
functions.logic: Accepts a vehicleId string and a date string in YYYY-MM-DD format. Executes a DuckDB query over the trip_events table to count distinct trip windows (grouped by hour) where vehicle_id matches and the event date matches the given date — this is actual_trips. Queries the expected_trip_windows table for the vehicle's scheduled windows on that date — this is expected_trips. Computes vt_ratio as actual_trips / expected_trips, clamped to a maximum of 1.0. If expected_trips is 0, returns vt_ratio of null and logs a warning. Emits a PostHog server-side event 'vehicle_vt_ratio_updated' with properties vehicle_id, date, vt_ratio, actual_trips, expected_trips using the PostHog server client. Returns the full result object. If vt_ratio is below 0.5, sets a flag in a Redis key 'vt_low_flag:{vehicleId}:{date}' with a 25-hour TTL so the 6AM WhatsApp briefing job can read it.

functions.name: enqueueActivationNudges
functions.signature: enqueueActivationNudges(operatorId: string, phoneNumber: string): Promise<{ job4hId: string; job24hId: string }>
functions.logic: Accepts an operatorId string and a phoneNumber string in E.164 format. Uses the Upstash Redis QStash client to enqueue two delayed HTTP jobs targeting the internal SMS dispatch endpoint '/api/internal/sms/send'. The first job is delayed by 14400 seconds (4 hours) with a payload of { operator_id: operatorId, phone: phoneNumber, template: 'gps_activation_hour4' }. The second job is delayed by 86400 seconds (24 hours) with a payload of { operator_id: operatorId, phone: phoneNumber, template: 'gps_activation_hour24_compliance' }. Stores both QStash message IDs in a Redis hash key 'nudge_jobs:{operatorId}' with fields 'job_4h' and 'job_24h' and a TTL of 30 hours. Returns the two job IDs. Throws if either enqueue fails so the caller can retry.

functions.name: cancelNudgeJobs
functions.logic: Accepts an operatorId string. Reads the Redis hash 'nudge_jobs:{operatorId}' to retrieve job_4h and job_24h QStash message IDs. For each non-null message ID, calls the QStash DELETE /v2/messages/{messageId} endpoint to cancel the pending job. Deletes the Redis hash key after cancellation. Returns { cancelled: N } where N is the number of successfully cancelled jobs (0, 1, or 2). Does not throw if a job ID is not found in QStash — this handles the case where the job already fired before cancellation was possible. Logs a warning if the Redis key does not exist, as this may indicate the operator never triggered nudge scheduling.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Parses the JSON body expecting operator_id (string) and plan_id (string). Checks Upstash Redis for an idempotency key 'mpesa_upgrade:{operator_id}:{plan_id}' — if present, returns 200 with the cached checkout_request_id to prevent duplicate STK pushes. Queries the ledger_events table for the operator's ledger_event_count and days_since_first_ping. Constructs the Daraja STK push request with the operator's registered M-Pesa phone number (from the operators table), the plan price in KES, and an account reference encoding ledger_event_count for contextual framing. Calls the Daraja StkPush API and on success stores the checkout_request_id in Redis with a 24-hour TTL under the idempotency key. Returns JSON 200 with { checkout_request_id, merchant_request_id }. On Daraja error, returns 502 with a structured error message.

integrations.description: Hyperledger Fabric network: GPS pings are written as signed ledger transactions via the Fabric SDK. The channel name and chaincode ID are configured via FABRIC_CHANNEL and FABRIC_CHAINCODE environment variables. A dead-letter queue (fabric_dlq table) handles write failures to maintain >99.5% success rate.

integrations.description: M-Pesa Daraja API: STK push upgrade flow initiated from the billing endpoint. Idempotency is enforced via Upstash Redis key scoped to operator_id + plan_id. Daraja credentials (DARAJA_CONSUMER_KEY, DARAJA_CONSUMER_SECRET, DARAJA_SHORTCODE, DARAJA_PASSKEY) must be set in environment.

telemetry.description: Fires on the very first GPS ping inserted into trip_events for a given vehicle and operator. This is the primary activation milestone for the GPS broadcast loop — it signals that the driver PWA is live, the device is broadcasting, and the operator has moved from zero-GPS to active tracking. Downstream: cancels SMS nudge jobs, unlocks full navigation, writes ledger genesis event, and starts the Day-28 upgrade gate countdown.

success_criteria: Time to First GPS Ping < 48 hours for > 60% of new operator accounts measured from account creation timestamp to first trip_events INSERT
Driver PWA load time < 4 seconds on Safaricom 3G (Chrome DevTools Slow 3G throttle profile)
Zero GPS ping loss rate: IndexedDB queue flush confirms 100% of pings enqueued offline are eventually delivered to trip_events
Hyperledger Fabric write success rate > 99.5% measured as (successful writeTripEvent calls) / (total GPS pings ingested) over any 7-day rolling window
V/T ratio > 0.75 across the active fleet portfolio at Month 2 post-launch, computed as average of all vehicle vt_ratio values from computeVTRatio
Free-tier ledger gate upgrade conversion > 15% measured as (operators who complete M-Pesa STK push after FreeTierLedgerGate prompt) / (operators who see the prompt)
Hour-4 SMS nudge delivery rate > 95% for operators with no GPS ping at T+4h
Fabric dead-letter queue (fabric_dlq) row count < 0.5% of total trip_events count at any point in time
GPS ping ingest endpoint p99 response latency < 500ms under normal load
Fleet Intelligence gate unlock rate: > 20% of operators with >= 5 active vehicles reach the 60-day ledger history threshold within 90 days of first GPS ping
